Ratio of the geometric to the arithmetic mean site size

Source: R/design.R
imbalance_ratio.Rd

Gives the ratio of the geometric to the arithmetic mean of the site sizes, the factor by which unequal sizes shrink the size that enters the informativeness, as a function of their coefficient of variation.

Usage

imbalance_ratio(cv, type = c("lognormal", "local"))

Arguments

cv

Coefficients of variation of the site sizes, numbers of at least 0.

type

"lognormal" (the default) for the exact ratio in a population of sizes (a lognormal population), \((1 + \mathrm{CV}^2)^{-1/2}\); "local" for the approximation \(\exp(-\mathrm{CV}^2/2)\) of a finite set of sizes close to their mean.

Value

A numeric vector of ratios, one per value of cv.

Details

The two are different statements (Lee, 2026, Appendix E.2). The lognormal ratio is an identity for a population; it does not give the geometric mean of a finite set of sizes from their coefficient of variation. The local approximation applies to a finite set, with an explicit remainder, when the sizes are close to their mean, and needs the coefficient of variation with divisor \(J\), not \(J - 1\). reliability_design() reports the exact ratio of a planned allocation. At a coefficient of variation of 0.75 the lognormal ratio is 0.80 and the local approximation 0.755.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

imbalance_ratio(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
#> [1] 0.9701425 0.8944272 0.8000000
imbalance_ratio(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), type = "local")
#> [1] 0.9692332 0.8824969 0.7548396
